# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

content.text:
I've mapped it. The app assumes in its core logic that every job has both apps, so this isn't only a change to the CTA. [Certain] Every point below comes from code I read.

**What breaks if the server sends a job without `learn_app` / `deliver_app`**
1. **Parsing fails.** `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:285-293`) calls `json.getJSONObject(META_LEARN_APP)` and the deliver equivalent. Those calls throw when the key is missing, so the job never reaches the device. `learn_progress` is required in the same way.
2. **Storage crashes.** `JobStoreManager.java:71-74, 278-318` writes and deletes both app records and learn modules unconditionally.
3. **Job status depends on learn progress.** `fromJson` (`:296-302`) sets LEARNING or DELIVERING from `getLearningPercentComplete`. That calls `passedAssessment()`, which reads `getLearnAppInfo().getPassingScore()` (`:657`). With no learn app, this crashes. Even with a null guard, the job could never leave AVAILABLE.
4. **About ten screens read app info directly.**
   - The job list checks whether each app is installed (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment.kt:151-152, 281`).
   - Intro and modules read `learnAppInfo.learnModules` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:158`, `ConnectLearnModulesBottomSheet.kt:40`).
   - Learn progress checks install state (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment.kt:120`, `ConnectLearnProgressView.kt:194`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView.kt:104`).
   - Delivery home does the same (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.kt:139, 185`).
5. **All CTAs go through one function.** `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp()` (`:439`) installs or launches the app. It's called from intro (after the start-learning API call), learn progress (including after claim), delivery home, the dashboard, and delivery "more". This is where the "open messaging" branch would go.
6. **Notifications.** Session-endpoint push notifications resolve an app ID per opportunity (`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity`, `FirebaseMessagingUtil.java:383`). Without apps, those would fail. Other notification types probably need checking too. [Likely]

**A gap on the messaging side**
`ConnectMessagingChannelRecord` has no field linking a channel to an opportunity. It only has `channel_source` and `channel_name`. So today the CTA can't open a specific conversation, only the channel list. [Certain] about the missing field; [Guessing] whether the server can add one.

**The question that shapes everything else**
On the learn and deliver screens, the progress bars, modules, assessment, and visit counts all come from activity in CommCare apps. If no app is involved, those screens have nothing to show unless something else supplies the data.

In this new opportunity type, what moves a worker from learning to delivering, and where do completed learning and delivery visits get recorded?

content.text:
You're partly right. The progress numbers come from the API. The module list, assessment, and passing score don't: they come from the `learn_app` object in that same payload, which is the thing that's going away.

[Certain] Here's where each piece comes from on the client:
- **Learn progress** (`completed_modules` / `total_modules`) and **delivery progress** (`deliver_progress`, plus the deliveries and payments APIs) come from the API. They don't depend on whether the app is installed.
- **The module list** on the Intro card and the modules sheet comes from `learn_app.learn_modules` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:158`).
- **The assessment passing score** comes from `learn_app.passing_score` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:657`).
- **Install state** is a local device check, used by the job list, delivery home, and the learn views.

**Your flow, as I understand it:** Intro (new opportunity) → Claim on the Intro page → job goes straight to DELIVERING → Delivery Home, whose CTA opens messaging. There's no learning phase at all. The channel ID will come later in the opportunity config; until then the CTA opens the channel list. [Guessing] on that interim behaviour.

**What this flow changes, beyond the null-safety work from before:**
1. **Status falls back after claiming. This is the main problem.** `ConnectRepository.kt:129` sets DELIVERING locally after a successful claim. But on the next sync, `fromJson` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`) recomputes status, and DELIVERING requires learning progress above 0. With no learn app, progress is 0, so a claimed job reverts to AVAILABLE and the worker lands back on Intro. For this opportunity type, the rule needs to become "claimed means delivering."
2. **The Intro CTA changes from start-learning to claim.** Today it calls `startLearning`, sets LEARNING, then `launchApp(isLearning = true)` (`ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:104-126`). It would call the claim API instead and go to Delivery Home. The claim call and its observer currently live in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro would need its own.
3. **Intro has to drop the learn-modules card**, or it shows 0 modules and 0 hours.
4. **"Revisit learning"** in `ConnectDeliveryMoreFragment.kt:48` needs to be hidden.
5. **Delivery Home's CTA** goes to messaging instead of `launchApp`. So does the "launch deliver app" action on the dashboard and the "more" screen.
6. **The claim API on the server** must allow claiming with no learning completed. I haven't checked the server code. [Guessing]

What's wrong or missing in that flow?

Also, should the app recognise this opportunity type from an explicit flag in the opportunity API (an opportunity type field, say), or just from `learn_app` and `deliver_app` being absent?

1. After a claim, server would return the status as delivery and we should respect that. Mostly we want to respect server Opp status everywhere and not make decisions locally. 3. drop the cards entirely 6. right

content.text:
The client doesn't read an opportunity status from the server today, so "respect server status" is a new contract with the server, not an existing one we can just honour. [Certain] `ConnectJobRecord.status` is stored under the `status` key, but `fromJson` never reads it. It always works the status out locally from learn progress and `claim` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`). The local overrides at `ConnectJobIntroFragment.kt:120` and `ConnectRepository.kt:129` are also local decisions. So this depends on the opportunity API sending a status value (available / learning / delivering, or similar). I haven't checked whether the server already sends one.

Noted:
- **3:** Intro drops the learn cards entirely for this type.
- **6:** The server's claim endpoint must allow claiming without any learning.

You said "everywhere," and that matters for scope. Applied only to the new type, server status is a contained change. Applied to all opportunities, it changes how existing learn/deliver jobs move between states. The local overrides after start-learning and claim would go away or become refresh-from-server. Older server versions or cached jobs without the field would need a fallback.

Should server-driven status apply only to this new no-app opportunity type, or replace the local status logic for every opportunity?
discard my statement, I didn't realise we don't get status from server but figure it out locally.

Understood. Status stays worked out on the device, so for this opportunity type the rule needs a new branch: **claimed means DELIVERING**, regardless of learn progress. Without it, a claimed job reverts to AVAILABLE on the next sync (`ConnectJobRecord.java:296-302`).

Here's the state handling for the no-app type, as I understand it:
- **Unclaimed** → AVAILABLE or AVAILABLE_NEW, as today. The job list shows it under new opportunities, and tapping it opens Intro.
- **Claim on Intro** → calls the existing claim API, sets DELIVERING locally (same as `ConnectRepository.kt:129` already does), and navigates to Delivery Home.
- **Next sync** → `fromJson` sees `claim` present and keeps DELIVERING because the job has no learn app.
- **LEARNING is never used** for this type, so the learn progress screen and the "revisit learning" entry are unreachable.
- **Expired or inactive** → the existing `isFinished()` handling applies unchanged. [Guessing] that finished no-app jobs should look the same in the list as other finished jobs.

What's wrong or missing there?

One question is still open from before: should the app recognise this opportunity type from an explicit field in the opportunity API, or just from `learn_app` and `deliver_app` being absent or null?
we will need to add  a new field on the Opportunity model called delivery_type which will be say "messaging" for this opportunity type

A new persisted field on `ConnectJobRecord` means a Connect DB migration. That's the riskiest mechanical part of this change, so it's worth planning for up front. [Certain] `ConnectJobRecord` is persisted, and adding a `@Persisting` field needs a DB version bump, a `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and an upgrade step, following the existing V2…V21 pattern.

The data model, as I understand it:
- **`delivery_type`** is a new string on the opportunity API. `"messaging"` means the no-app type. If it's absent or has any other value, the job is treated as today's learn/deliver type, so older servers and existing cached jobs keep working. [Guessing] on the default; tell me if the server will always send it.

# Messaging-delivery opportunities (no learn or deliver app)

## Intent

Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity that has no CommCare app at all: no learn app and no
deliver app. The worker reads the Intro page, claims the opportunity, and from then on works through
PersonalID messaging. The Connect pages still exist, but nothing on them installs or launches a
CommCare app; the primary CTA opens messaging instead.

Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.

## Goals

- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "messaging"` parse, store, and display without crashing.
- Flow: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → status DELIVERING → Delivery Home, whose CTA opens
  PersonalID messaging.
- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today.

## Non-goals

- Opening a specific messaging channel. The server will later add a channel id to the opportunity
  config; until then the CTA opens the messaging channel list.
- Server-driven opportunity status. Status remains derived on the device.
- Server changes (the claim endpoint accepting a claim with no learning, sending `delivery_type`).
  These are prerequisites owned by the server team.

## Anti-goals

- Inferring the type from `learn_app` / `deliver_app` being null. The type comes only from
  `delivery_type`.
- Any regression in the existing learn → claim → deliver flow, including for jobs cached before the
  upgrade.

## Server contract

On the opportunity list API, for a messaging opportunity:

- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other value means
  the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `learn_app`: `null`.
- `deliver_app`: `null`.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today.

Other APIs:

- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
- Claim API: called from Intro; the server accepts it with no learning completed.
- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.

## Design

### Data model and storage

- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`), plus a single
  predicate on the record (e.g. `isMessagingDelivery()`). Every branch below checks this predicate.
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30), add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and add an
  upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with the default type.
  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`: read `learn_app` and `deliver_app` as nullable; both app records stay
  null when the JSON value is null.
- `JobStoreManager` (store and delete paths, learn module writes) and
  `ConnectJobUtils` (`getCompositeJob` module attach, `getAppIdForOpportunity`) skip absent app
  records instead of dereferencing them.

### Status

Status stays derived locally in `fromJson`. Add a branch: for a messaging job, `claim` present →
`STATUS_DELIVERING`; otherwise `STATUS_AVAILABLE`. A messaging job never enters `STATUS_LEARNING`.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
app.

### Screens

| Screen | Change for messaging jobs |
|---|---|
| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | No app-installed checks; no app record lookup for last-accessed date. |
| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | CTA claims the job instead of start-learning. On success, set DELIVERING locally (as `ConnectRepository.claimJob` already does) and navigate to Delivery Home. Learn cards are dropped entirely. |
| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging via `ConnectNavHelper.goToMessaging` (no channel id for now). No install-state checks. Skip `loadLearningProgress`. |
| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open and "launch deliver app" actions don't call `launchApp`; "revisit learning" is hidden. |
| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | A non-delivering messaging job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |

The claim call and its observer currently live in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`; Intro needs
the same claim handling (loading, error, success) on its own ViewModel.

### Learn progress API guard

Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

### Notifications

Push flows that resolve an app id per opportunity (`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity`, used
by session-endpoint notifications in `FirebaseMessagingUtil`) must handle a job with no apps without
crashing.

## Builder's discretion

- Exact name and form of the type predicate and the default value constant.
- Whether app-launch branching lives in `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp` or in each CTA handler.
- CTA label strings for Claim and messaging. Use `dev-utils:add-mobile-string` for new strings.
- Test structure, following AGENTS.md: unit tests for parsing, status, and migration; Robolectric UI
  tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home and the messaging CTA.
- Updating `docs/connect/` with a short note on the messaging delivery type.

# PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities

## Intent

Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity in which delivery happens through PersonalID messaging
instead of a CommCare deliver app. These opportunities never have a deliver app. They may or may not
have a learn app:

- **With a learn app:** learning works as today. After claiming, the worker goes to Delivery Home,
  whose CTA opens messaging instead of a deliver app.
- **Without a learn app:** the worker reads Intro, claims from Intro, and goes straight to Delivery
  Home with the messaging CTA.

Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.

## Goals

- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "personalid_messaging"` parse, store, and display without
  crashing, with or without a learn app.
- Without a learn app: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the
  messaging CTA.
- With a learn app: job list → Intro → start learning → learn app → learn progress → claim →
  DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the messaging CTA.
- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today.

## Non-goals

- Opening a specific messaging channel. The server will later add a channel id to the opportunity
  config; until then the CTA opens the messaging channel list.
- Server-driven opportunity status. Status remains derived on the device.
- Server changes (the claim endpoint accepting a claim with no learning when there is no learn app,
  sending `delivery_type`). These are prerequisites owned by the server team.

## Server contract

On the opportunity list API, for a PersonalID messaging opportunity:

- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"personalid_messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other
  value means the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `deliver_app`: always `null`.
- `learn_app`: an app object, or `null` when the opportunity has no learn app.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today.

Other APIs:

- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
- Claim API: called from Intro when there is no learn app, and from learn progress (as today) when
  there is one. Without a learn app, the server accepts the claim with no learning completed.
- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.

## Design

### Data model and storage

- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`). Branches use two
  checks on the record:
  - **PersonalID messaging delivery** (`deliveryType == "personalid_messaging"`): governs everything
    on the delivery side (deliver app, Delivery Home CTA, tasks).
  - **Has learn app** (`learnAppInfo != null`): governs everything on the learn side (Intro learn
    cards, start learning vs. claim, learn progress API, revisit learning).
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30), add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and add an
  upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with the default type.
  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`:
  - PersonalID messaging job: `learn_app` is nullable. `deliver_app` is ignored and the deliver app
    record is always null, even if the server sends one. *(Our call.)*
  - Any other job: a null or missing `learn_app` or `deliver_app` is rejected as malformed (throws,
    so `ConnectOpportunitiesParser` skips the job as it does other bad entries). This keeps
    learn/deliver paths free of null guards. *(Our call.)*
- `JobStoreManager` (store and delete paths, learn module writes) and `ConnectJobUtils`
  (`getAppIdForOpportunity`) skip absent app records instead of dereferencing them.

### Status

Status is set locally in four places:

| Where | What it does | PersonalID messaging change |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` | Derives AVAILABLE / LEARNING / DELIVERING from learn progress and `claim`. | New branch, below. |
| `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` | Keeps the stored status if it is further along than the parsed one; marks newly seen AVAILABLE jobs AVAILABLE_NEW. | None. |
| `ConnectJobIntroFragment` start-learning success | Sets LEARNING. | Unchanged with a learn app; not reached without one. |
| `ConnectRepository.claimJob` success | Sets DELIVERING. | None; both claim entry points reuse it. |

`fromJson` branch for PersonalID messaging jobs:

1. `claim` present → DELIVERING.
2. Otherwise, has a learn app and learn progress > 0 → LEARNING.
3. Otherwise → AVAILABLE.

Without a learn app the job never enters LEARNING. The claim rule is needed because the
no-regression rule in `storeOrUpdateJob` only protects a device that recorded the claim locally. A
fresh install, a second device, or a claim made outside this device would otherwise derive
AVAILABLE and show Intro for a claimed job.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
app.

### Screens

| Screen | With learn app | Without learn app |
|---|---|---|
| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | Learning entries as today. Delivering entries skip the deliver-app install check and last-accessed lookup. | No app install checks or last-accessed lookups. |
| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | As today: learn cards shown, CTA starts learning. | Learn cards dropped entirely. CTA claims the job, then navigates to Delivery Home. |
| Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`) | Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label. | Not reached. |
| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging via `ConnectNavHelper.goToMessaging` (no channel id for now). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today. | Same, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped. |
| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today. | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden. |
| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | As today. | A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |

For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently
lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.

Where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record that is absent,
they read them from the job record and use the existing card styles. No new card design. *(Our
call.)*

### Tasks

PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through
`ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:

- **Conversation task** (`isOCSConversation`): unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
- **Any other task**: shows an error toast, "No action found for the task", instead of launching
  the deliver app. No navigation.
- The More tab's pending-task badge is unchanged.

**Delivery Home CTA enablement.** Today's rule
(`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment.updateCtaBarEnabled`) is: the CTA is disabled only when the deliver
app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.

For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is
disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending
non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays
blocked until the server clears the task.

### Learn progress API guard

Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

### Notifications

`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in
`FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns no app id when the requested app is absent: always for delivery
status, and for learn status when there is no learn app. The caller drops the notification as it
already does when the app id can't be resolved.

## Builder's discretion

- Exact names of the two checks and the delivery type constant.
- Whether app-launch branching lives in `BaseConnectFragment.launchApp` or in each CTA handler.
- CTA label strings for Claim and messaging. Use `dev-utils:add-mobile-string` for new strings.
- Test structure, following AGENTS.md: unit tests for parsing (both variants), status, and
  migration; Robolectric UI tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home, learn-complete claim → Delivery
  Home, and the messaging CTA.
- Updating `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

## Overview

Reviews an implementation plan, breaks it into logically independent tickets, and creates them in Jira with descriptions, implementation details, and Backlog status. It works best if the plan is supplied as a Github link. 

## Process

### Step 1: Review the Plan

Read the full implementation plan. Identify logical breakpoints using these criteria (in priority order):

2. **max ~500 lines per PR** — keeps PRs easy to review; split further if a ticket would exceed this

### Step 2: Ask About Custom Fields

Before creating any tickets, ask the user:

> "Would you like to populate additional ticket fields (e.g components)?"

- **Yes** → ask for each field value one at a time before creating tickets

- **Description**: Overview of the changes
- **Status**: Backlog

To create the tickets I need you to sign in to Atlassian first: run `/mcp` and select **claude.ai Atlassian MCP**. Once you're signed in I'll look up the field IDs for the Connect Mobile team and the "Mobile team - Sprint 102" sprint, and use CCCT-2860 as the parent and `mobile` as the component.

I checked the breakdown against every section of the spec. It was missing three things, and I've added them:
- **Job list cards for opportunities with no app record.** The card's description and organization come from the job record. Added to ticket 4.
- **The two new CTAs that set `lastWorkedDate`.** The messaging CTA and the Intro claim CTA don't exist until tickets 5 and 6, so ticket 1 can't wire them up. Added to tickets 5 and 6.
- **The `docs/connect/` note** about the messaging delivery type. Added to ticket 5.

Every other section of the spec maps to exactly one ticket.

Here's the final list. Each ticket body will also include its spec sections copied word for word.

**1. Sort Connect job list by last worked date**
- *What it does:* Each section of the job list shows the opportunity the worker last worked on first. Tapping a learn or delivery button marks the opportunity as worked on now.
- *Covers:*
  - Remove the unused `isAppInstalled` checks and field.
  - Replace the `processJobRecords` / `lastAccessed` sort with `lastWorkedDate`, newest first.
  - Keep `lastWorkedDate` across syncs in `storeOrUpdateJob`.
  - Set it on the existing CTAs: Intro start learning, learn progress continue, learn-complete claim, Delivery Home, revisit learning, and task taps.
- *Spec:* Job list ordering; the job list row in Screens.

**2. Fix crash when opening a messaging channel that isn't stored locally**
- *What it does:* Opening messaging for a channel that hasn't synced to the device shows the channel list instead of crashing.
- *Covers:* a null check in `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` before `selectChannel`.
- *Spec:* Messaging CTA, the null-channel item.

**3. Store delivery type and launch slug on Connect opportunities**
- *What it does:* The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields: the delivery type, and the messaging channel for opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging. Nothing uses them yet.
- *Covers:*
  - Parse `delivery_type` and `launch.slug`.
  - Persist `deliveryType` and `launchSlug`.
  - `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` 30 → 31, with a `ConnectJobRecordV31` snapshot, upgrader backfill, and retargeted earlier migrations.
- *Spec:* Data model and storage (fields and migration).

**4. Handle opportunities without learn or deliver apps safely**
- *What it does:* Opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging sync and show in the job list without crashing, with or without a learn app. Malformed opportunities are skipped.
- *Covers:*
  - Rules in `fromJson` for which app objects are allowed or required.
  - The new status branch.
  - Guarding `passedAssessment`.
  - Null handling in `storeAppInfo`, `storeModules`, and `pruneOldJobs`.
  - Job list card description and organization when the app record is missing.
  - The learn progress API guard.
  - `getAppIdForOpportunity` returning null, and the notification code dropping the notification.
- *Spec:* Data model and storage (parsing and `JobStoreManager`), Opportunity Status, Learn progress API guard, Notifications, and the job list card note in Screens.

**5. Messaging delivery for opportunities with a learn app**
- *What it does:* After finishing learning and claiming, the worker goes to Delivery Home, and its button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of a CommCare app. Tasks that need an app show "No action found for the task", and pending tasks disable the button.
- *Covers:*
  - Learn-complete claim → Delivery Home, using the "go to delivery" label.
  - Delivery Home messaging CTA via `unlockAndGoToMessaging(launchSlug)`, which also sets `lastWorkedDate`.
  - Remove deliver-app install checks.
  - The More tab's deliver-app launch action.
  - Task toast and CTA enablement rules.
  - Robolectric tests for learn-complete claim → Delivery Home and the messaging CTA.
  - The `docs/connect/` note.
- *Spec:* Screens (Learn progress, Delivery Home, Delivery dashboard / more), Messaging CTA, Tasks, Delivery Home CTA.

**6. Messaging delivery for opportunities without a learn app**
- *What it does:* The worker claims straight from Intro and lands on Delivery Home with the messaging button. Learning content is hidden throughout.
- *Covers:*
  - Intro: claim CTA and ViewModel claim handling, hide the learn cards, and set `lastWorkedDate` on claim.
  - `handleInfoRedirect` → Intro for non-delivering jobs.
  - Hide revisit learning.
  - Robolectric test for Intro claim → Delivery Home.
- *Spec:* Screens (Intro, Delivery dashboard / more, `handleInfoRedirect`); claim handling in Intro.

1	# PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities
2	
3	## Intent
4	
5	Connect is adding a new kind of opportunity in which delivery happens through PersonalID messaging
6	instead of a CommCare deliver app. These opportunities never have a deliver app. They may or may not
7	have a learn app:
8	
9	- **With a learn app:** learning works as today. After claiming, the worker goes to Delivery Home,
10	  whose CTA opens messaging instead of a deliver app.
11	- **Without a learn app:** the worker reads Intro, claims from Intro, and goes straight to Delivery
12	  Home with the messaging CTA.
13	
14	Today the mobile app assumes every opportunity has both apps. Parsing, storage, status derivation,
15	and most Connect screens dereference `learnAppInfo` / `deliveryAppInfo` unconditionally, so an
16	opportunity without them either fails to parse or crashes.
17	
18	## Goals
19	
20	- Opportunities with `delivery_type = "personalid_messaging"` parse, store, and display without
21	  crashing, with or without a learn app.
22	- Without a learn app: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the
23	  messaging CTA.
24	- With a learn app: job list → Intro → start learning → learn app → learn progress → claim →
25	  DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the messaging CTA.
26	- The status stays DELIVERING across syncs after claim.
27	- Existing learn/deliver opportunities behave exactly as today, except job list ordering (see
28	  **Job list ordering**), which changes for all opportunities.
29	
30	
31	## Server contract
32	
33	On the opportunity list API, for a PersonalID messaging opportunity:
34	
35	- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"personalid_messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other
36	  value means the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
37	- `deliver_app`: always `null` when delivery_type is "personalid_messaging".
38	- `learn_app`: an app object, or `null` when the opportunity has no learn app.
39	- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today but API is only called when learn app is present. 
40	- `launch.slug`: new nested field holding the messaging channel id the Delivery Home CTA opens.
41	  `launch` or `slug` would be absent or empty for non PersonalID messaging opportunities.
42	
43	Other APIs:
44	
45	- Learn progress API: the client must never call it for a job whose `learnAppInfo` is null.
46	- Claim API: called from Intro when there is no learn app, and from learn progress (as today) when
47	  there is one. Without a learn app, the server accepts the claim with no learning completed.
48	- Delivery progress, deliveries, and payments APIs: unchanged.
49	
50	## Design
51	
52	### Data model and storage
53	
54	- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`). Branches use two
55	  checks on the record:
56	  - **PersonalID messaging delivery** (`deliveryType == "personalid_messaging"`): governs everything
57	    on the delivery side (deliver app, Delivery Home CTA, tasks).
58	  - **Has learn app** (`learnAppInfo != null`): governs everything on the learn side (Intro learn
59	    cards, start learning vs. claim, learn progress API, revisit learning).
60	- Add a persisted `launchSlug` field (`launch_slug`), parsed from `launch.slug` (empty when absent).
61	- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30) once for both new fields, add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>`
62	  snapshot, and add an upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with
63	  the default type and an empty channel id.
64	  Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot,
65	  following the existing V2…V21 pattern.
66	- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`:
67	  - PersonalID messaging job: `learn_app` is nullable. `deliver_app`
68	    record is always null, validate and reject as malformed if not. 
69	  - Any other job: a null or missing `learn_app` or `deliver_app` is rejected as malformed (throws,
70	    so `ConnectOpportunitiesParser` skips the job as it does other bad entries). This keeps
71	    learn/deliver paths free of null guards. *(Our call.)*
72	- `JobStoreManager`. Stored app records and learn modules mirror the server, and no step reads
73	  fields of an app record that is null:
74	  - `storeAppInfo`: an app that is present is written as today. When `learnAppInfo` or
75	    `deliveryAppInfo` is null, any stored record of that kind for the job is deleted and nothing is
76	    written. Without the delete, `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs`, which attaches every stored app
77	    record matching the job UUID, would bring back a learn app the server has removed.
78	  - `storeModules`: a null `learnAppInfo` counts as an empty incoming module list. The existing
79	    prune step deletes the job's stored modules, and nothing is written. Modules only arrive inside
80	    `learn_app.learn_modules`.
81	  - `pruneOldJobs`: when deleting a job the server no longer sends, it collects IDs only from app
82	    records that are present. Module IDs come from `learnAppInfo` when it is present. Without a
83	    learn app the job has no stored modules, because `storeModules` keeps them empty.
84	
85	### Opportunity Status
86	
87	Opportunity Status is set locally in four places:
88	
89	| Where | What it does | PersonalID messaging change |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson` | Derives AVAILABLE / LEARNING / DELIVERING from learn progress and `claim`. | New branch, below. |
92	| `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` | Keeps the stored status if it is further along than the parsed one; marks newly seen AVAILABLE jobs AVAILABLE_NEW. | None. |
93	| `ConnectJobIntroFragment` start-learning success | Sets LEARNING. | Unchanged with a learn app; not reached without one. |
94	| `ConnectRepository.claimJob` success | Sets DELIVERING. | None; both claim entry points reuse it. |
95	
96	`fromJson` branch for PersonalID messaging jobs:
97	
98	1. `claim` present → DELIVERING.
99	2. Otherwise, has a learn app and learn progress > 0 → LEARNING.
100	3. Otherwise → AVAILABLE.
101	
102	Without a learn app the job never enters LEARNING. The claim rule is needed because the
103	no-regression rule in `storeOrUpdateJob` only protects a device that recorded the claim locally. A
104	fresh install, a second device, or a claim made outside this device would otherwise derive
105	AVAILABLE and show Intro for a claimed job.
106	
107	`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn
108	app.
109	
110	### Screens
111	
112	| Screen | With learn app                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Without learn app |
113	|---|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---|
114	| Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`) | For all jobs: remove the unused `isAppInstalled` checks and the unused `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field (nothing reads it), and sort as in **Job list ordering**. No app record lookups remain. | Same. |
115	| Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`) | As today: learn cards shown, CTA starts learning.                                                                                                                                                              | Learn cards dropped entirely. CTA claims the job, then navigates to Delivery Home. |
116	| Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`) | For Messaging opportunities, Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label.              | Not reached. |
117	| Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`) | CTA opens messaging (see **Messaging CTA**). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today.                                                                                              | Same, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped. |
118	| Delivery dashboard / more | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today.                                                                                                                                          | Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden. |
119	| `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect` | As today.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen. |
120	
121	For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently
122	lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.
123	
124	At places where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record, 
125	we would read them from the job record when app record is absent.
126	
127	### Job list ordering
128	
129	Applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.
130	
131	- Each job list section sorts by `ConnectJobRecord.lastWorkedDate`, most recent first. This replaces
132	  the sort by the linked app's `lastAccessed` (`processJobRecords`), which was ascending
133	  (least recent first) and only updated on CommCare app login.
134	- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now whenever the user taps a learn or delivery CTA for the job:
135	  - Intro CTA (start learning, or claim when there is no learn app)
136	  - Learn progress continue CTA
137	  - Learn-complete claim CTA
138	  - Delivery Home CTA (deliver app or messaging)
139	  - "Revisit learning"
140	  - Task taps on the dashboard and More tabs
141	- `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the
142	  stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status
143	  from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
144	- Logging into a CommCare app directly (not through a Connect CTA) no longer affects ordering.
145	- `lastWorkedDate` is already persisted; no migration needed for it.
146	
147	### Messaging CTA
148	
149	- Opens messaging through `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging` with the job's
150	  `launchSlug`, matching how conversation tasks open their channel.
151	- Empty channel id → opens the messaging channel list.
152	- Channel id not yet in the local messaging DB (for example, right after claim, before messages
153	  sync) → stays on the channel list and shows a toast, "Channel doesn't exist". Today
154	  `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the lookup result straight to
155	  `selectChannel`, which crashes on null. The fix belongs there, so it also covers conversation
156	  tasks.
157	- Consent is handled by the existing channel screen (`ConnectMessageFragment`); no change.
158	
159	### Tasks
160	
161	PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through
162	`ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:
163	
164	- **Conversation task** : unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
165	- **Any other task**: shows an error toast when there is no app present -  "No action found for the task".
166	
167	### Delivery Home CTA 
168	
169	Today the CTA is disabled only when the deliver
170	app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.
171	
172	For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is
173	disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending
174	non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays
175	blocked until the server clears the task.
176	
177	### Learn progress API guard
178	
179	Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call.
180	This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.
181	
182	### Notifications
183	
184	`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in
185	`FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns null when the requested app is absent. `handleSessionEndpointNotification` treats null
186	like its existing unresolved-app case and returns null, so no notification is shown.
187	
188	## Other
189	
190	- Robolectric UI tests for Intro claim → Delivery Home, learn-complete claim → Delivery
191	  Home, and the messaging CTA.
192	- Update `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

## Overview
Each section of the Connect job list shows the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first. Tapping any learn or delivery button on an opportunity marks it as worked on now. Applies to all opportunities, and also removes unused app-install checks from the job list.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Screens: Job list (`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`)**
For all jobs: remove the unused `isAppInstalled` checks and the unused `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field (nothing reads it), and sort as in **Job list ordering**. No app record lookups remain.

**Job list ordering**

Applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

- Each job list section sorts by `ConnectJobRecord.lastWorkedDate`, most recent first. This replaces the sort by the linked app's `lastAccessed` (`processJobRecords`), which was ascending (least recent first) and only updated on CommCare app login.
- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now whenever the user taps a learn or delivery CTA for the job:
  - Intro CTA (start learning, or claim when there is no learn app)
  - Learn progress continue CTA
  - Learn-complete claim CTA
  - Delivery Home CTA (deliver app or messaging)
  - "Revisit learning"
  - Task taps on the dashboard and More tabs
- `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
- Logging into a CommCare app directly (not through a Connect CTA) no longer affects ordering.
- `lastWorkedDate` is already persisted; no migration needed for it.

Scope note: this ticket wires the CTAs that exist today. The Intro claim CTA and the messaging Delivery Home CTA are added in the PersonalID messaging tickets, which set `lastWorkedDate` themselves.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each job list section is ordered by `lastWorkedDate`, most recent first
- [ ] Tapping any existing learn/delivery CTA or a task updates `lastWorkedDate` and moves the opportunity to the top of its section
- [ ] `lastWorkedDate` survives an opportunity sync
- [ ] `isAppInstalled` checks, the `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field and the `lastAccessed` lookup are removed from the job list

input.summary: Fix crash when opening a messaging channel that isn't stored locally
input.description:
## Overview
When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`), **Messaging CTA**:

- Channel id not yet in the local messaging DB (for example, right after claim, before messages sync) → stays on the channel list and shows a toast, "Channel doesn't exist". Today `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the lookup result straight to `selectChannel`, which crashes on null. The fix belongs there, so it also covers conversation tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Opening messaging with a channel id that isn't in the local messaging DB shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast
- [ ] Opening messaging with a stored channel id still opens that channel
- [ ] No crash from `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` for an unknown channel id

input.summary: Store delivery type and launch slug on Connect opportunities
input.description:
## Overview
The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields from the server: the delivery type (identifies opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging) and the launch slug (the messaging channel those opportunities open). Nothing uses them yet; this lays the data groundwork with a single Connect DB migration.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Server contract** (opportunity list API)
- `delivery_type`: new string field. `"personalid_messaging"` marks this type. Absent or any other value means the existing learn/deliver type (older servers, existing cached jobs).
- `launch.slug`: new nested field holding the messaging channel id the Delivery Home CTA opens. `launch` or `slug` would be absent or empty for non PersonalID messaging opportunities.

**Data model and storage**
- Add a persisted `deliveryType` field to `ConnectJobRecord` (`delivery_type`). Branches use two checks on the record:
  - **PersonalID messaging delivery** (`deliveryType == "personalid_messaging"`): governs everything on the delivery side (deliver app, Delivery Home CTA, tasks).
  - **Has learn app** (`learnAppInfo != null`): governs everything on the learn side (Intro learn cards, start learning vs. claim, learn progress API, revisit learning).
- Add a persisted `launchSlug` field (`launch_slug`), parsed from `launch.slug` (empty when absent).
- Bump `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` (currently 30) once for both new fields, add the `ConnectJobRecordV<N>` snapshot, and add an upgrade step in `ConnectDatabaseUpgrader` that backfills existing rows with the default type and an empty channel id. Prior migrations that targeted `ConnectJobRecord.class` must be retargeted to the new snapshot, following the existing V2…V21 pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `delivery_type` and `launch.slug` are parsed into `deliveryType` and `launchSlug` and persisted
- [ ] Missing fields default to the learn/deliver type and an empty slug
- [ ] Upgrading from Connect DB version 30 keeps existing jobs and backfills the defaults
- [ ] Migration unit test covers the upgrade

input.summary: Handle opportunities without learn or deliver apps safely
input.description:
## Overview
Opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging (no deliver app, learn app optional) sync, are stored, get the right status, and appear in the job list without crashing. Malformed opportunities are skipped, and notifications that point at a missing app are dropped.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Server contract** (opportunity list API, PersonalID messaging opportunity)
- `deliver_app`: always `null` when delivery_type is "personalid_messaging".
- `learn_app`: an app object, or `null` when the opportunity has no learn app.
- `learn_progress`: still present; parsed as today but API is only called when learn app is present.

**Data model and storage**
- `ConnectJobRecord.fromJson`:
  - PersonalID messaging job: `learn_app` is nullable. `deliver_app` record is always null, validate and reject as malformed if not.
  - Any other job: a null or missing `learn_app` or `deliver_app` is rejected as malformed (throws, so `ConnectOpportunitiesParser` skips the job as it does other bad entries). This keeps learn/deliver paths free of null guards.
- `JobStoreManager`. Stored app records and learn modules mirror the server, and no step reads fields of an app record that is null:
  - `storeAppInfo`: an app that is present is written as today. When `learnAppInfo` or `deliveryAppInfo` is null, any stored record of that kind for the job is deleted and nothing is written. Without the delete, `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs`, which attaches every stored app record matching the job UUID, would bring back a learn app the server has removed.
  - `storeModules`: a null `learnAppInfo` counts as an empty incoming module list. The existing prune step deletes the job's stored modules, and nothing is written. Modules only arrive inside `learn_app.learn_modules`.
  - `pruneOldJobs`: when deleting a job the server no longer sends, it collects IDs only from app records that are present. Module IDs come from `learnAppInfo` when it is present. Without a learn app the job has no stored modules, because `storeModules` keeps them empty.

**Opportunity Status**

`fromJson` branch for PersonalID messaging jobs:
1. `claim` present → DELIVERING.
2. Otherwise, has a learn app and learn progress > 0 → LEARNING.
3. Otherwise → AVAILABLE.

Without a learn app the job never enters LEARNING. The claim rule is needed because the no-regression rule in `storeOrUpdateJob` only protects a device that recorded the claim locally. A fresh install, a second device, or a claim made outside this device would otherwise derive AVAILABLE and show Intro for a claimed job.

`passedAssessment()` reads `learnAppInfo.passingScore`, so it must not run for jobs without a learn app.

**Screens (job list cards)**
At places where job list cards would read description and organization from an app record, we would read them from the job record when app record is absent.

**Learn progress API guard**
Guard inside `ConnectRepository.getLearningProgress`: if `learnAppInfo` is null, don't make the call. This covers Delivery Home's `loadLearningProgress` and any future caller.

**Notifications**
`ConnectJobUtils.getAppIdForOpportunity` (used by session-endpoint notifications in `FirebaseMessagingUtil`) returns null when the requested app is absent. `handleSessionEndpointNotification` treats null like its existing unresolved-app case and returns null, so no notification is shown.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PersonalID messaging opportunities with and without a learn app parse, store and show in the job list without crashing
- [ ] A PersonalID messaging opportunity with a non-null `deliver_app`, or any other opportunity with a missing app, is skipped as malformed
- [ ] Claimed PersonalID messaging opportunities derive DELIVERING on a fresh sync
- [ ] Removing a learn app on the server removes the stored learn app record and modules
- [ ] Learn progress API is never called for a job without a learn app
- [ ] Session-endpoint notifications for a missing app are dropped without a crash
- [ ] Unit tests cover parsing (both variants), status derivation and storage

input.summary: Messaging delivery for opportunities with a learn app
input.description:
## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Tasks that need an app show "No action found for the task", and pending tasks disable the button. Depends on the delivery type/launch slug and null-safety tickets.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Screens**
- Learn progress (`ConnectLearningProgressFragment`, `ConnectLearnCompleteView`): For Messaging opportunities, Claim success always navigates to Delivery Home; never launches a deliver app. The learn-complete CTA uses the "go to delivery" label, never the download-app label.
- Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`): CTA opens messaging (see **Messaging CTA**). No deliver-app install checks. `loadLearningProgress` runs as today (skipped without a learn app via the learn progress API guard).
- Delivery dashboard / more: Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" shown as today.

**Messaging CTA**
- Opens messaging through `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging` with the job's `launchSlug`, matching how conversation tasks open their channel.
- Empty channel id → opens the messaging channel list.
- Consent is handled by the existing channel screen (`ConnectMessageFragment`); no change.

**Tasks**
PersonalID messaging jobs can have pending tasks. Opening one goes through `ConnectTaskPresenter.open` from the dashboard and More tabs:
- **Conversation task**: unchanged. Opens messaging on the task's channel.
- **Any other task**: shows an error toast when there is no app present - "No action found for the task".

**Delivery Home CTA**
Today the CTA is disabled only when the deliver app is installed **and** at least one task is pending. Otherwise it is enabled.

For PersonalID messaging jobs, the messaging CTA counts as an installed deliver app: **the CTA is disabled while any task is pending, and enabled otherwise.** Accepted risk: a pending non-conversation task blocks the CTA, and tapping it only shows the toast, so the worker stays blocked until the server clears the task.

**Job list ordering**
- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now when the user taps the messaging Delivery Home CTA.

**Other**
- Robolectric UI tests for learn-complete claim → Delivery Home and the messaging CTA.
- Update `docs/connect/` with a short note on the PersonalID messaging delivery type.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Learn-complete claim on a PersonalID messaging opportunity navigates to Delivery Home and never starts a deliver app download
- [ ] Learn-complete CTA shows the "go to delivery" label for these opportunities
- [ ] Delivery Home CTA opens the `launchSlug` channel, or the channel list when the slug is empty, and updates `lastWorkedDate`
- [ ] Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; conversation tasks open their channel
- [ ] Delivery Home CTA is disabled while any task is pending
- [ ] No deliver-app code path runs for PersonalID messaging opportunities
- [ ] Robolectric tests and `docs/connect/` note added

input.summary: Messaging delivery for opportunities without a learn app
input.description:
## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities with no learn app, the worker reads the Intro page, claims directly from it, and lands on Delivery Home with the messaging button. Learning content (learn cards, revisit learning, learn progress screen) is never shown. Depends on the null-safety and "with a learn app" messaging tickets.

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Goals**
- Without a learn app: job list → Intro → **Claim** on Intro → DELIVERING → Delivery Home with the messaging CTA.

**Server contract**
- Claim API: called from Intro when there is no learn app, and from learn progress (as today) when there is one. Without a learn app, the server accepts the claim with no learning completed.

**Screens (without learn app)**
- Intro (`ConnectJobIntroFragment`): Learn cards dropped entirely. CTA claims the job, then navigates to Delivery Home.
- Delivery Home (`ConnectDeliveryHomeFragment`): Same as with a learn app, but `loadLearningProgress` is skipped.
- Delivery dashboard / more: Task open handled as in **Tasks**. "Revisit learning" hidden.
- `ConnectActivity.handleInfoRedirect`: A non-delivering job routes to Intro, not the learn progress screen.

For jobs without a learn app, Intro needs claim handling (loading, error, success). It currently lives only in `ConnectLearningProgressViewModel`, so Intro's ViewModel needs the same handling.

**Opportunity Status**
- `ConnectRepository.claimJob` success sets DELIVERING; both claim entry points reuse it.

**Job list ordering**
- `lastWorkedDate` is set to now when the user taps the Intro claim CTA.

**Other**
- Robolectric UI test for Intro claim → Delivery Home.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Intro for a PersonalID messaging opportunity without a learn app shows no learn cards and a claim CTA
- [ ] Claiming from Intro shows loading/error states, sets DELIVERING, updates `lastWorkedDate` and navigates to Delivery Home
- [ ] "Revisit learning" is hidden and the learn progress screen is never reached
- [ ] `handleInfoRedirect` sends a non-delivering opportunity to Intro
- [ ] Robolectric test for Intro claim → Delivery Home added

## Implementation

From the mobile spec for PersonalID messaging delivery opportunities (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md`):

**Screens: Job list (**`ConnectOpportunityListFragment`)  
For all jobs: remove the unused `isAppInstalled` checks and the unused `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field (nothing reads it), and sort as in **Job list ordering**. No app record lookups remain.

**Job list ordering**

Applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

* Each job list section sorts by `ConnectJobRecord.lastWorkedDate`, most recent first. This replaces the sort by the linked app's `lastAccessed` (`processJobRecords`), which was ascending (least recent first) and only updated on CommCare app login.
* `lastWorkedDate` is set to now whenever the user taps a learn or delivery CTA for the job:

    * Intro CTA (start learning, or claim when there is no learn app)
    * Learn progress continue CTA
    * Learn-complete claim CTA
    * Delivery Home CTA (deliver app or messaging)
    * "Revisit learning"
    * Task taps on the dashboard and More tabs
    
* `last_worked` from the server stays unparsed. `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` copies the stored `lastWorkedDate` onto the incoming record before writing, the same way it keeps status from going backwards. A newly seen job keeps the constructor default (first sync time).
* Logging into a CommCare app directly (not through a Connect CTA) no longer affects ordering.
* `lastWorkedDate` is already persisted; no migration needed for it.

Scope note: this ticket wires the CTAs that exist today. The Intro claim CTA and the messaging Delivery Home CTA are added in the PersonalID messaging tickets, which set `lastWorkedDate` themselves.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] Each job list section is ordered by `lastWorkedDate`, most recent first
* \[ \] Tapping any existing learn/delivery CTA or a task updates `lastWorkedDate` and moves the opportunity to the top of its section
* \[ \] `lastWorkedDate` survives an opportunity sync
* \[ \] `isAppInstalled` checks, the `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` field and the `lastAccessed` lookup are removed from the job list

## Overview
When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation
When messaging is asked to open a channel, check that the channel exists on the device first. If it does, open it as today; if not, stay on the channel list and show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

Spec: [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Opening a channel that isn't on the device shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
- Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

## Overview
The app reads and stores two new opportunity fields from the server: the delivery type, which marks opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging, and the launch slug, which is the messaging channel those opportunities open. Nothing uses them yet.

## Implementation
Parse both fields from the opportunity API and save them with the opportunity, using a single Connect database upgrade. Opportunities from older servers, and ones already on the device, default to the existing learn/deliver type with no channel.

Spec: [Server contract](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#server-contract), [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Delivery type and launch slug are saved with each opportunity
- Existing opportunities keep working after the app upgrade and get the defaults
- The database upgrade is covered by a test

## Overview
Opportunities delivered through PersonalID messaging (never a deliver app, learn app optional) sync, are stored, get the right status, and show in the job list without crashing.

## Implementation
- Accept a missing learn app and require no deliver app for PersonalID messaging opportunities; skip any other opportunity whose apps are missing as malformed.
- Keep stored app and learning-module data in line with what the server sends, including removing a learn app the server has dropped.
- A claimed PersonalID messaging opportunity is always in delivery, even on a fresh install or a second device.
- Never request learning progress for an opportunity without a learn app.
- Job list cards fall back to the opportunity's own description and organization.
- Notifications that point at a missing app are dropped.

Spec: [Data model and storage](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#data-model-and-storage), [Opportunity Status](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#opportunity-status), [Learn progress API guard](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#learn-progress-api-guard), [Notifications](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#notifications)

## Acceptance Criteria
- PersonalID messaging opportunities, with and without a learn app, sync and show in the job list without crashing
- Malformed opportunities are skipped
- Claimed PersonalID messaging opportunities show as in delivery after any sync
- No learning progress request for opportunities without a learn app
- Notifications for a missing app are dropped without a crash

## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities, after finishing learning and claiming, the worker lands on Delivery Home, whose main button opens their PersonalID messaging channel instead of downloading or launching a CommCare deliver app. Depends on CCCT-2996 and CCCT-2997.

## Implementation
- After claiming from the learning-complete screen, go straight to Delivery Home; the button reads "go to delivery", never "download app".
- Delivery Home's main button opens the opportunity's messaging channel, or the channel list when none is set.
- Tasks: conversation tasks open their channel as today; any other task shows "No action found for the task". The main button stays disabled while any task is pending.
- Nothing in the delivery screens tries to install or launch a deliver app.
- Add UI tests and a short note to the Connect docs.

Spec: [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens), [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta), [Tasks](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#tasks), [Delivery Home CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#delivery-home-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claiming after learning lands on Delivery Home with no deliver app download
- Delivery Home's button opens the opportunity's messaging channel
- Non-conversation tasks show "No action found for the task"; the button is disabled while tasks are pending
- UI tests and docs note added

## Overview
For PersonalID messaging opportunities with no learn app, the worker reads the Intro page, claims directly from it, and lands on Delivery Home with the messaging button. Learning content is never shown. Depends on CCCT-2997 and CCCT-2998.

## Implementation
- Intro hides the learning cards and its button claims the opportunity, with loading and error states, then opens Delivery Home.
- Opening an unclaimed opportunity of this kind always goes to Intro, never the learning screen.
- "Revisit learning" is hidden on the delivery screens.
- Add a UI test for claiming from Intro.

Spec: [Goals](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#goals), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Intro shows no learning cards and a claim button
- Claiming from Intro lands on Delivery Home
- Learning screens and "Revisit learning" are never shown
- UI test added

   - **`ConnectJobRecord`**
     - Status is worked out on the device in `fromJson`; the server's status is not used.
     - `STATUS_AVAILABLE_NEW`/`AVAILABLE`/`LEARNING`/`DELIVERING`.
     - `JobStoreManager.storeOrUpdateJob` never lets a stored status go backwards, and marks newly seen jobs as `AVAILABLE_NEW`.
   - **`ConnectAppRecord`** holds learn/deliver app info. Learn modules exist only inside `learn_app.learn_modules`. `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs` attaches every stored app record that matches the job UUID.
   - **Connect DB:** `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` = 30. Migrations use versioned snapshot classes (`ConnectJobRecordV2…V21`). Per a memory note, earlier migrations must be retargeted to the new snapshot.
   - **`lastAccessed`:** a local `ConnectLinkedAppRecord` field, set on CommCare app login through `PostLoginSideEffects`. It is used only for job-list sorting, and that sort was ascending.
   - **`lastWorkedDate`:** `ConnectJobRecord` sets it to `new Date()` in the constructor. `fromJson` never reads `last_worked` from the server, and `storeOrUpdateJob` overwrites the stored value on every sync.
   - **Dead install flag:** `ConnectLoginJobListModel.isAppInstalled` is assigned but never read.
   - **Messaging navigation:** `ConnectNavHelper.unlockAndGoToMessaging(activity, policy, channelId, listener)`.
   - **Existing null-channel crash:** `ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.onViewCreated` passes the channel lookup straight to `selectChannel`, which crashes when the channel isn't stored locally.
   - **Tasks:** `ConnectTaskPresenter.open`. A non-conversation task launches the deliver app.
