content.text:
Today each section of the job list is sorted by the linked CommCare app's `lastAccessed`, oldest first, so the opportunity you used least recently is at the top. [Certain] The code is in `app/src/org/commcare/fragments/connect/ConnectOpportunityListFragment.kt:176-183`.

**How it works:**
- There are three sections: In progress, New and Finished. Each one is sorted with `sortBy { it.lastAccessed }`, which is ascending.
- In progress: completed-delivery jobs are sorted separately and added at the end.
- The sort value comes from `processJobRecords` (line 233). It finds the job's app (the learn app for learning rows, the deliver app for delivery, new and finished rows) and reads that app's `ConnectLinkedAppRecord.lastAccessed`.
- That value is only written in two places:
  - When the linked app record is first created (`ConnectLinkedAppRecord.java:75`).
  - On CommCare app login (`PostLoginSideEffects.kt:42` → `ConnectAppUtils.updateLastAccessed`).
- If the app has no linked record (never installed or logged into), it uses `Date()`, the time the list was built. Those jobs end up at the bottom, below every job that has a record. Among themselves they come out in the order they were processed, because the timestamps are all nearly the same.

**What this means:**
- **New:** most new jobs have no linked record, so this section is effectively in database order.
- **In progress:** sorted by when you last logged into the learn or deliver app, oldest first.

The spec's **Job list ordering** section matches this: it replaces the sort with `lastWorkedDate`, most recent first.

content.text:
No, there's no sync triggered because the channel is missing. Today the app crashes before any sync can start. [Certain]

**What happens today** (`app/src/org/commcare/fragments/connectMessaging/ConnectMessageChannelListFragment.java`):
1. `goToMessaging` opens `ConnectMessagingActivity` with the channel id and does no lookup or sync of its own (`ConnectNavHelper.kt:55`).
2. `onViewCreated` (line 76) looks the channel up in the local DB only. When it isn't found, `getMessagingChannel` returns null, and `selectChannel(null)` calls `channel.getChannelId()`, which throws a NullPointerException.
3. A full message sync, `MessageManager.retrieveMessages`, runs in `onResume` (line 98) on every visit to the channel list. But `onResume` comes after `onViewCreated`, so in the missing-channel case it never gets that far.

**With the fix in the spec (toast, stay on the list):** the screen survives, so the `onResume` sync now runs and `refreshUi` adds the new channel to the list. [Certain] That sync is the normal one every list visit does, not one triggered by the missing channel.

**Gap in the spec:** the lookup happens before the sync, so right after a claim (the exact case the spec describes) the worker would see "Channel doesn't exist". A second later the channel shows up in the list, but it doesn't open on its own. The toast would be wrong at that point and the worker would have to tap the channel.

What I'd do instead: when the channel isn't found locally, wait for the `retrieveMessages` result, then look the channel up again. Open it if it's there now, and show "Channel doesn't exist" only if it's still missing (or the sync failed). This is a small change in the same fragment and covers conversation tasks as well. ## Overview

When the app opens messaging for a specific channel that hasn't synced to the device yet (for example, right after claiming, or from a conversation task), it fetches the latest messages and opens the channel once it arrives. If the channel still doesn't exist, the worker stays on the channel list and sees a "Channel doesn't exist" toast instead of the app crashing.

## Implementation

When messaging is asked to open a channel, check whether the channel exists on the device. If it does, open it as today. If not, stay on the channel list, wait for the messages sync to finish, and check again: open the channel if it now exists, otherwise show the toast. This covers both the new messaging button and existing conversation tasks.

Spec: [Messaging CTA](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#messaging-cta)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Opening a channel that isn't on the device but arrives in the messages sync opens that channel
* Opening a channel that is still missing after the sync, or when the sync fails, shows the channel list and a "Channel doesn't exist" toast, with no crash
* Opening a channel that is on the device still opens it

content.text:
No, null learn and deliver apps don't need a DB update. [Certain]

**Why:**
- `learnAppInfo` and `deliveryAppInfo` on `ConnectJobRecord` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:183-184`) aren't persisted columns. They have no `@Persisting` annotation and are transient fields.
- Each app is stored as its own row in the `ConnectAppRecord` table. Those rows are keyed by job UUID and have an `isLearning` flag (`ConnectAppRecord.java:35-67`).
- When a job is loaded, `ConnectJobUtils.populateJobs` attaches whichever rows match the job.
- So "no learn app" just means there's no learn row for that job. The schema already supports this.

**What does need handling** is the storage code, and **CCCT-2997** covers it (spec section *Data model and storage*, the `JobStoreManager` rules):
- `storeAppInfo` deletes the stored row of that kind when the app is null, so `populateJobs` can't bring back a stale learn app.
- `storeModules` treats a null learn app as an empty module list.
- `pruneOldJobs` skips null apps when it collects IDs to delete.

The only DB migration in this work is in **CCCT-2996**: the `DB_VERSION_CONNECT` bump that adds the `deliveryType` and `launchSlug` columns to `ConnectJobRecord`.

## Overview

Today each section of the job list is sorted by the linked CommCare app's lastAccessed, oldest first, so the opportunity you used least recently is at the top. Instead each section of the Connect job list should show the opportunity the worker most recently worked on first, and keep that order on a fresh sign-in or a second device. This applies to all opportunities, not only PersonalID messaging ones.

## Implementation

Read the server's new last active time for each opportunity. Also record the time a worker taps any learn or delivery button (start learning, continue learning, claim, go to delivery, revisit learning, open a task) on an opportunity. On each sync keep whichever of the device and server times is more recent, and sort each job list section by it, newest first. An opportunity the worker has never worked on sorts below worked ones. Logging into a CommCare app directly no longer affects the order. Also remove the unused app-installed checks from the job list.

Depends on the server exposing `last_active` on the opportunity list API.

Spec: [Server contract](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#server-contract), [Job list ordering](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#job-list-ordering), [Screens](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-android/blob/c32ee32ad8735689108e461e5f0570ea01de70cd/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-messaging-delivery-opportunity-design.md#screens)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Each job list section is ordered by last worked time, most recent first
* Tapping a learn or delivery button, or a task, moves that opportunity to the top of its section
* The order survives an opportunity sync
* On a fresh sign-in the order follows the server's last active times
* A server time later than the device's time replaces it; an earlier one does not
* Opportunities with no last active time sort below worked ones

Keeping the newer of the two times has one catch: as the code stands, the server value would never win on a fresh sign-in. [Certain] The `ConnectJobRecord` constructor sets `lastWorkedDate = new Date()` (`ConnectJobRecord.java:194`), so a newly parsed job always has a device time of "now", which is later than any server timestamp. To fix this, the spec now has `fromJson` set `lastWorkedDate` from `last_active`, and to the epoch (1970) when `last_active` is absent or null. That also puts never-worked jobs below worked ones, rather than at the top with the time of the first sync.

**Spec changes (local only):**
- *Server contract:* adds `last_active` as a new nullable timestamp on every opportunity, not just messaging ones. It needs server work.
- *Job list ordering:*
  - `fromJson` reads `last_active`, and uses the epoch when it's missing.
  - `storeOrUpdateJob` keeps whichever of the stored and incoming `lastWorkedDate` is more recent.
  - Tapping a learn or delivery button still sets the time on the device.
  - Accepted risk: device clock and server clock are compared directly, so a device with a wrong clock can order jobs incorrectly.
  - `lastWorkedDate` is already a persisted column, so there's still no migration.

**CCCT-2994:**
- The description now covers the server value and the newer-wins rule, and notes that it depends on the server exposing `last_active`.
- It links the Server contract section.
- It has three new acceptance criteria:
  - The order follows the server on a fresh sign-in.
  - The device time is replaced only by a later server time.
  - Jobs with no last active time sort at the bottom.

No ticket covers exposing `last_active` on the server. Do you want me to create a web/server ticket under CCCT-2860 for it? The links still point to `c32ee32` until you push the spec.
